propositions: No AST gate currently validates that only approved composition roots and provider boundaries read ambient config and credentials; below-seam load_config/os.getenv/os.environ reads and unowned credential names can silently appear.

An AST gate must detect six prohibited categories (ambient env read, helper-shim env read, load_config calls, getattr env equivalents, provider-credential reads outside boundary, backend registry access below provider boundary) only when the enclosing module is not an approved seam for that category.

Owner sets for credentials and environments must be derived at runtime from existing registries (_child_env.owned_secret_names, _ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES, gen_env_registry.scan, _deprecations.REGISTRY, and @register decorators) rather than hand-copied, and path-glob exceptions must be structurally rejected.

Receiver-object aliasing (e.g., src=os.environ; src.get('SECRET')) and callee aliasing (import/local-assign forms) must be resolved before classification so direct and indirect access forms classify consistently.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry's scan/KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS/matchers directly (single source); unresolved dynamic env reads and shim-shaped callees absent from the helper table must fail closed as unresolved-env-read.
A legacy-exception registry with exact path+symbol+rationale entries must cover current below-seam reads to make the gate introducible without touching product code; C3 drains exceptions to empty.
